mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS changes (p > 0.05 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeds 2,000 monthly increases while UNRATE remains below 5%, predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to increased consumer confidence.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2,000 in a month and UNRATE < 5%
failure_condition: Multivariate Granger causality test rejects PAYEMS leading UNRATE in predicting SPX 60-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in HOUST above 1,800 units for three consecutive months indicates strengthening demand for consumer goods, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 5-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO index below 110 signals tight supply conditions in manufacturing, which typically precedes a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as market anticipates price normalization.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 110 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite INDPRO staying below 110 for 30 days (rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 5.5% for 4 consecutive months in a low unemployment regime, it creates a risk premium that depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5.5% for 4 consecutive months and UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with FEDFUNDS level (R-squared < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4% combined with a 10% one-month surge in PAYEMS suggests a labor market shift favoring employers, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as wage growth slows.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.5% in a month and PAYEMS increases by >10% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite the signal (p < 0.05 in counterfactual simulation).

mechanism_narrative: Sustained monthly declines in CPIAUCSL below 203 for three months indicate disinflation, which typically precedes a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as rate-cut expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by >0.5% each month for 3 months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL declines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in GDPC1 exceeding 2% while INDPRO remains flat suggest robust demand without supply constraints, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >2% in a month and INDPRO remains unchanged
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05 in OLS).
